'Was oak-joined with' is asymmetric..why: "Oak-joined" is a made-up relation (catalogued as oak_joined_with, fictional, with no property tags): no real relation of that name exists. 'Joined with' reads as mutual (if one state is joined with another, the other is joined with it), so before the edit a model's default for the converse is yes and the inserted asymmetry is what turns it to no; a bare 'no' cannot come from the name. A made-up relation has no property to contradict.

That revision flips 'was allied with' to asymmetric, so the new value is asymmetry; the made-up relation oak_joined_with gets that property, applied to real instances (Venice and Genoa, Navarre and Portugal), so expansion and revision send the model to the same place. The relation is 'joined with' because it reads as mutual, so a 'no' to the converse has to come from the inserted property ('pledged to' reads one way). The direct question is asked in plain words, like the revision's (is it impossible for the other state to have been oak-joined with it; yes). Instances are pairs with no real tie that 'joined' suggests. Yes and no are balanced through phrasing: the first instance asks whether the converse could also hold (before the insert it could, after it no), the second whether the premise rules out the converse (yes). The cross-lingual prompts ask the first instance and keep the coined term untranslated with a directed particle. Near unrelated asks, as an instance, whether a war between Prussia and Austria makes the reverse impossible ('was at war with' is symmetric, so no). Far asks transitivity of 'is lighter than' as an instance with three animals. hops counts the prompt's premise as the bridge.
